newsitem.title: INDIA: Around 350 feared dead in mid-air collision - PTI.
newsitem.headline: Around 350 feared dead in mid-air collision - PTI.

text.p: Nearly 350 people were feared dead on Tuesday when a Saudi Arabian jumbo jet and a Kazakhstan airliner collided in mid-air west of New Delhi, the Press Trust of India (PTI) reported.
Aviation officials told Reuters there were 312 people, including crew, aboard the Saudi Boeing 747 and 39, including 10 crew, on the other aircraft.
"There is hardly any chance of survivors," one official said.
If the toll is confirmed, the air disaster will be among the world's five worst for loss of life and the worst involving two aircraft in flight.
Initial reports were sketchy but one aviation source said: "It was like a bolt of lightning and two streaks of fire descended down to the ground."
The collision occurred shortly before 7.00 p.m. (1330 GMT) as night was falling over India.

PTI said: "Nearly 350 passengers were feared killed when a Saudi Airways jumbo jet and a Kazakhstan airliner collided in mid-air about 40 nautical miles west of Delhi this evening, according to civil aviation sources."
"I saw a ball of flame hurtling down and I could make out that it was an aircraft," it quoted one eyewitness as saying.
Earlier, PTI said a Saudi Arabian Boeing 747 collided with a Kazakh Airways TU-154 aircraft and heavy casualties were feared.
The agency said the collision occurred over Jhajhar in the Rohtak district of Haryana state bordering New Delhi. Aviation officials told Reuters the accident occurred at Charkhi Dadri.
The area, west of New Delhi, has scattered villages.
PTI quoted airport sources as saying the Saudi Arabian Airlines Corp plane, with a flight number of SV 763, had been bound for Dhahran and Jeddah in Saudi Arabia.
It quoted the sources as saying the Kazakh plane, believed to be a Russian-built TU-154, with flight number KZA 1907, was travelling from Kazakhstan to New Delhi.
The agency quoted the sources as saying the wreckage of the two aircraft was spread over a wide area.
PTI quoted officials of the directorate general of civil aviation as saying the Saudi airliner had been cleared to climb to a flight level of 14,000 feet by air traffic control in New Delhi.
It said the Kazakh airliner had been cleared to descend to 15,000 feet on the same route.
PTI said the radar blips of both aircraft disappeared seven minutes after the Saudi airliner left New Delhi.
